'''''Pavonia hastata''''', commonly known as '''spearleaf swampmallow'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=PAHA5|taxon=Pavonia hastata|accessdate=15 September 2015}}</ref> or '''pink pavonia''', is a shrub in the family [[Malvaceae]].<ref name=ANPSA>{{cite web|title=''Pavonia hastata''|publisher=Australian Native Plants Society (Australia)|url=http://anpsa.org.au/p-has.html|access-date=8 January 2012|archive-date=12 August 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120812062419/http://anpsa.org.au/p-has.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

==Distribution==
The species is native to Brazil, Bolivia, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay.<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate=15 April 2017}}</ref> It was previously considered to be native to Australia as well, but is no longer thought to be.<ref name="ANPSA"/>

==Description==
[[File:Pavonia hastata Tokyo.jpg|thumb|left|Growing at roadside]]
A spreading [[subshrub]] or shrub, the plant grows to 1.5 metre high and have leaves that are 10 to 60 mm long and 10 to 25 mm wide. Leaves [[Glossary of botanical terms|ovate]] to oblong with heart-shaped or willow-shaped base, toothed, rough-haired on the upper side, hairy on the lower side, 1-6 cm long, 1-2.5 cm wide with 3 cm long petioles. 

===Inflorescence===
The hibiscus-like flowers are pink with a red throat. Flowers solitary in the [[leaf axil]]s, on petioles shorter than the leaves. Outer lining almost as long as the lining, hairy. [[Petal]]s up to 1.2 cm long, white to reddish purple with dark basal spot. [[Stamen]]s gave 12 pieces. The first flowers in spring are often [[cleistogamous]] and much smaller than those that come later in the season. Flowering occurs profusely during summer and autumn.<ref name=NSW>{{cite web |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Pavonia~hastata|title=''Pavonia hastata'' L. |access-date=8 January 2013 |author=|work= PlantNET - New South Wales Flora Online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens & Domain Trust, Sydney Australia}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
The species is easily propagated by seed or cuttings.<ref name="ANPSA"/>
